becomes the peritubular capillary circulation.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q012.takeaway: Albumin is the first major plasma protein to appear with barrier injury because its effective molecular size approaches the filtration cutoff.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q012.displayText:
Albumin is the first major plasma protein to appear with barrier injury because its effective molecular size approaches the filtration cutoff.

In renal diseases, albumin is the first to appear because of its effective molecular diameter.
In minimal change nephropathy, the negative charges on the basement membrane are lost even
before there are noticeable changes in kidney histology. As a result of this loss of negative charges
on the basement membranes, some of the lower molecular weight proteins, especially albumin
(effective molecular diameter of 7 nm), are filtered and appear in the urine, a condition known as

proteinuria or albuminuria.
emphasis: Albumin is the first major plasma protein to appear with barrier injury because its effective molecular size approaches the filtration cutoff

rationales.a: Albumin concentration is high but concentration alone does not determine selective leakage across the damaged barrier.
rationales.c: The albumin-to-globulin ratio does not explain selective filtration; molecular size/charge barriers do.
rationales.d: Epithelial sensitivity is not the filtration-barrier mechanism responsible for albuminuria.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q017.takeaway: Renal sympathetic activation constricts afferent arterioles, lowering renal blood flow and GFR.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q017.displayText:
Renal sympathetic activation constricts afferent arterioles, lowering renal blood flow and GFR.

GFR decreases with sympathetic stimulation as there is afferent arteriolar constriction.
Strong activation. of the renal 8ynipathetic nerves constrict the afferent and efferent renal
arteriolesthrough the ° 1 receptors. As the afferent areterioles have far more ° 1 receptors than the
efferent, it results in decreased renal blood flow and GFR.
emphasis: Renal sympathetic activation constricts afferent arterioles, lowering renal blood flow and GFR

rationales.a: Afferent dilation increases glomerular inflow and is not the usual sympathetic response.
rationales.b: Efferent dilation lowers glomerular capillary pressure; it is not the principal sympathetic mechanism.
rationales.d: Efferent constriction tends to raise glomerular pressure initially; sympathetic effect described is afferent constriction.
